questions.enonce_markdown:
Define the following terms as used in genetics,

i) Homozygous.

ii) Heterozygous.

iii) Recessive.

iv) Dominance. *(2,2,2,1 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Homozygous:** having **two identical alleles** of a gene for a characteristic, e.g. $RR$ or $rr$ (a pure breed).

(ii) **Heterozygous:** having **two different alleles** of a gene for a characteristic, e.g. $Rr$ (a hybrid).

(iii) **Recessive:** an allele whose effect is **hidden (masked) in the presence of a dominant allele**; it shows only in the **homozygous** condition, e.g. $rr$.

(iv) **Dominance:** the ability of an allele to **express itself in the phenotype in the heterozygous condition**, masking the effect of the other allele.

questions.enonce_markdown:
A farmer grows plants with rose flowers that are either red in colour or white. He realized that there was a quest for pink coloured roses. In an attempt to get the pink coloured roses, he crossed the pure breed rose flowered red plant with the pure breed white flowered plant.

Using genetic symbols and diagrams explain the results of this cross. *(7 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The pink colour shows that neither allele is completely dominant over the other: this is **incomplete dominance** (the heterozygote has an intermediate phenotype).

**Key:** $C^R$ = allele for red flowers; $C^W$ = allele for white flowers.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Parental phenotypes** | Red flowers $\times$ White flowers |
| **Parental genotypes** | $C^RC^R$ $\times$ $C^WC^W$ (pure breeds, homozygous) |
| **Gametes** | all $C^R$ and all $C^W$ |

**Punnett square:**

| | $C^R$ | $C^R$ |
|---|---|---|
| **$C^W$** | $C^RC^W$ | $C^RC^W$ |
| **$C^W$** | $C^RC^W$ | $C^RC^W$ |

**F1 genotype:** all $C^RC^W$ (heterozygous). **F1 phenotype:** **all pink** flowers (100 %).

The farmer therefore gets pink roses in the first generation.

questions.enonce_markdown: What would be the outcome of a cross between the pink flowers and the red parent? *(6 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Parental phenotypes:** pink $\times$ red

**Parental genotypes:** $C^RC^W$ $\times$ $C^RC^R$

**Gametes:** $C^R$ and $C^W$ (from the pink parent); all $C^R$ (from the red parent)

**Punnett square:**

| | $C^R$ | $C^W$ |
|---|---|---|
| **$C^R$** | $C^RC^R$ | $C^RC^W$ |
| **$C^R$** | $C^RC^R$ | $C^RC^W$ |

**Offspring genotypes:** 2 $C^RC^R$ : 2 $C^RC^W$, that is 1 : 1.

**Offspring phenotypes:** **red : pink = 1 : 1**, so **50 % red flowers and 50 % pink flowers**; no white flowers are produced.
